36 In the circuits shown, the batteries are identical and all have negligible internal resistance. All of
the resistors have the same resistance. The diodes have zero resistance when conducting and
infinite resistance when not conducting.
In which circuit is the current in the battery greatest?
A
B
C
D

hints: Notice the diode direction in each branch: a diode is zero resistance if conventional current can pass from its triangle to its bar, and infinite resistance if reversed.
For the same battery e.m.f. $V$, battery current is $I = V/R_{total}$, so compare the effective resistance seen by the battery after removing blocked branches.
Check how many resistors of resistance $R$ remain in parallel in A versus C and D, and what happens to the single series loop in B.
walkthrough: The batteries have the same e.m.f. $V$ and negligible internal resistance, so battery current is $I = V/R_{total}$ where $R_{total}$ is the effective resistance of the conducting resistors.
Treat a conducting diode as a wire of zero resistance and a non-conducting diode as a break of infinite resistance. A branch with a reverse-biased diode carries no current.
In A both parallel branches have diodes pointing to allow current through the resistors, so two resistances $R$ are in parallel. Total resistance is $R_{total} = R/2$ and $I = V/(R/2) = 2V/R$.
In B the resistors and diodes are all in one series loop but the diodes point in opposite senses, so one must be reverse-biased. The loop is open, $R_{total}$ is infinite and $I = 0$.

In C the left branch is a plain resistor $R$ and the right branch diode is reverse-biased, so only one $R$ is connected. $R_{total} = R$ and $I = V/R$. In D one parallel branch conducts and the other is blocked, so again $R_{total} = R$ and $I = V/R$.
Comparing $2V/R$ with $V/R$ and $0$ shows the smallest total resistance and greatest battery current is in the two-branch conducting circuit. This is option A.

A.explanation: Both parallel branches have forward-biased diodes, so both resistors conduct and total resistance is $R/2$, giving the largest battery current.

B.explanation: The two diodes oppose each other in the single series loop, so one diode blocks and the battery current is zero.

C.explanation: Only the plain resistor branch conducts because the diode branch is reverse-biased, so total resistance is $R$, larger than in A.

D.explanation: One parallel diode is forward-biased and one is reverse-biased, so only one resistor conducts and total resistance is $R$.
